title: Tight Security Bounds for Cascade and Xor-Cascade Encryption
summary: Provable security bounds for cascade and xor-cascade encryption are weaker than known distinguishing-attack lower bounds; tightening them to match remains open.

formal_statement.body: In the random-system framework, cascade encryption and xor-cascade encryption have provable security bounds that are weaker than known distinguishing-attack lower bounds. For xor-cascade encryption, the relevant comparison distinguishes odd and even cascade lengths $l$, with a particularly stated case for $l\in\{3,4\}$. The open task is to determine whether the provable security bounds for both constructions can be tightened to match those stronger lower bounds, including the odd/even length cases and the $l\in\{3,4\}$ cases.

scope.domain: Security bounds for cascade and xor-cascade block-cipher constructions.
assumptions: The bounds are considered in the random-system framework.
parameters: l: xor-cascade length, with separate odd and even cases and a highlighted case of l in {3, 4}
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the provable security bounds for both constructions can be tightened to match the stronger lower bounds, including the stated xor-cascade length cases.

citations.label: Towards Key-Length Extension with Optimal Security: Cascade Encryption and Xor-cascade Encryption

progress.summary: The source notes that known distinguishing-attack lower bounds are tighter than the bounds proved for the two cascade constructions. Closing this gap, including the odd and even xor-cascade length cases, remains unresolved.
citation_labels: Jooyoung Lee et al., Towards Key-Length Extension with Optimal Security: Cascade Encryption and Xor-cascade Encryption
